title: Progressive Refinement: An Iterative Pseudo-Labeling Approach for Mandarin-English Code-Switching ASR
gist: Apple researchers apply iterative pseudo-labeling to Mandarin-English code-switching automatic speech recognition for the first time, using a three-phase pipeline (pseudo-label generation, two-stage bilingual training, iterative refinement) to cut Mix Error Rate by 6.35% on SEAME's devman subset and 8.29% on devsge.

themes.theme: Data scarcity as the core code-switching ASR problem

insights.claim: Code-switching, alternating languages within the same utterance, poses significant challenges for automatic speech recognition because of limited training data specific to code-switched speech, distinct from the data available for monolingual ASR.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Voice-assistant makers serving bilingual populations (e.g., Mandarin-English speakers) face a data-availability constraint that generic ASR scaling doesn't solve, making techniques for leveraging unlabeled data strategically important for product quality in these markets.
insights.quote: Code-switching (CS), alternating languages within the same utterance, poses significant challenges for automatic speech recognition (ASR) due to limited CS training data.

insights.claim: This is the first application of an iterative pseudo-labeling training approach to code-switching ASR, and it demonstrates that pseudo-labeling can effectively leverage large amounts of unlabeled data to improve performance on this task.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Establishing pseudo-labeling as effective for code-switching ASR opens a lower-cost path (using unlabeled audio instead of expensive labeled code-switched transcripts) for other language pairs facing the same data-scarcity constraint.
insights.quote: This paper applies an iterative pseudo-labeling training approach to CS-ASR for the first time, demonstrating its effectiveness in leveraging unlabeled data to improve CS-ASR performance.

insights.claim: The approach comprises three phases: generating pseudo-labels from a large unlabeled corpus to create a semi-supervised dataset, a two-stage bilingual model training framework (pre-training then fine-tuning on supervised code-switching data), and further iterative refinements to improve accuracy on complex code-switching scenarios.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The three-phase pipeline (pseudo-label generation, two-stage training, iterative refinement) is a reusable template that other teams building bilingual or multilingual ASR systems could adopt directly.
insights.quote: The approach comprises three phases: pseudo-label generation, two-stage bilingual model training, and iterative improvements.

themes.theme: Measured accuracy gains on a standard benchmark

insights.claim: The iterative pseudo-labeling approach achieved Mix Error Rate reductions of 6.35% on SEAME's devman subset and 8.29% on its devsge subset, giving a concrete, benchmarked accuracy gain for Mandarin-English code-switching ASR.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A benchmarked ~6-8% MER reduction on a recognized standard (SEAME) gives product and research teams a quantifiable target to beat or a technique to adopt for improving bilingual voice-assistant accuracy.
insights.quote: achieving notable Mix Error Rate (MER) reductions on SEAME's devman (6.35%) and devsge (8.29%) subsets
